58:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Mujadalah In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, who said: Praise be to God, Whose hearing encompasses all sounds. A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him, and I was in a corner of the house, unable to hear what she was saying. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband to the end of the verse. Al-Bukhari narrated it in this way in the Book of Monotheism, as a suspended narration, and he said: Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, and he mentioned it. An-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir narrated it through different chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. In a narration by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aishah that she said: Blessed be He whose hearing has absorbed everything. I hear the words of Khawlah bint Tha’labah, and some of them are hidden from me, as she complains about her husband to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she says: O Messenger of God, he has consumed my wealth, wasted my youth, and scattered my belly for him, until I have grown old and my children have ceased to be with me. O God, I complain to You. She said: I did not stop until Gabriel came down with this verse: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband. She said: And her husband is Aws ibn al-Samit. Ibn Lahi'ah said on the authority of Abu al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah that he is Aws ibn al-Samit. Aws was a man who had a affliction, and whenever his affliction seized him and became severe, he would pronounce zihar declaration of divorce from his wife, but when it went away, he did not say anything. So she came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to ask him about that and complain to God, so God revealed: "God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God" 1:13. And thus Hisham ibn Urwah narrated on the authority of his father that a man had a affliction, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Musa ibn Ismail Abu Salamah told us: Jarir, meaning Ibn Hazim, told us: I heard Abu Yazid narrating: I met the wife of Umar, whose name was Khawlah bint Tha'labah, and he was walking with the people, so she stopped him. He stopped for her, approached her, lowered his head to her, and placed his hands on her shoulders until she had satisfied her need and left. A man said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, you have detained the men of Quraysh for this old woman. He said: Woe to you, do you know who this is? He said: No. He said, “This is a woman whose complaint God heard from above the seven heavens. This is Khawlah bint Tha’labah. By God, if she did not leave me until nightfall, I would not leave her until she had satisfied her need, unless the time for prayer came, so I could pray it and then return to her until she had satisfied her need.” This is disconnected between Abu Yazid and Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it has been narrated from other chains of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan told us, Ya’la told us, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Amir, who said: The woman who argued about her husband was Khawlah bint as-Samit, and her mother was Mu’adhah, about whom God revealed, And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity. The correct version is Khawlah, the wife of Aws ibn as-Samit.
58:2: Imam Ahmad said: Sa`d ibn Ibrahim and Ya`qub told us: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Mu`ammar ibn `Abdullah ibn Hanzala told me, on the authority of Yusuf ibn `Abdullah ibn Salam, on the authority of Khuwaylah bint Tha`labah, who said: By God, God revealed the beginning of Surat Al-Mujadilah about me and Aws ibn al-Samit. She said: I was with him and he was a very old man whose character had become bad. She said: One day he came to me and I asked him something, so he became angry and said: You are to me like the back of my mother. She said: Then he went out and sat in the gathering of his people for an hour, then he came in to me and behold, he wanted to have intercourse with me. She said: I said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is Khawlah’s soul, you will not be able to get to me, and I have said what I have said, until God and His Messenger judge us with His judgment. She said: Then he jumped on me, and I resisted him, and I overcame him as a woman overcame a weak old man, and I threw him off me. She said: Then I went out to one of my female neighbors and borrowed some clothes from her, then I went out until I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and sat in front of him, and I mentioned to him what I had suffered from him and I began to complain to him about the bad character I had suffered from him. She said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) began to say: Khawlah, your cousin is an old man, so fear God regarding him. She said: By God, I did not leave until a verse was revealed in the Qur’an, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was overcome by what had always overwhelmed him, then he recovered and said to me: O Khuwaylah, God has revealed a Qur’an about you and your companion. Then he recited to me: “God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. Those among you who swear to divorce their wives, they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say an ugly saying and a lie. And indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who swear to divorce their wives and then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch each other. This is what you are admonished to do, and God is Acquainted with what you do. But whoever cannot find [the means], then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. But whoever is not able [to do so], then the feeding of sixty poor persons. This is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger. And these are the limits set by God. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.” She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Tell him to free a slave. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, what does he have?” He said: Then let him fast for two consecutive months. She said: “I said: By God, he is an old man who has no time for fasting.” He said: Then let him feed sixty poor people a wasq of dates. She said: “I said: By God, O Messenger of God, he does not have that.” She said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then we will help him with a vessel of dates.’” She said: “I said: O Messenger of God, and I will help him with another vessel.” He said: You have done well and done well, so go and give it in charity on his behalf, then treat your cousin well. She said: So I did that. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Divorce in his Sunan through two chains of transmission on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, and he has Khawlah bint Tha’laba, and it is said that she is Khawlah bint Malik ibn Tha’laba, and it may be made diminutive and it is said that she is Khawila. There is no contradiction between these statements, so the matter is close, and God knows best. This is the correct explanation for the reason for the revelation of this Surah. As for the hadith of Salamah ibn Sakhr, it does not state that it was the reason for the revelation, but rather it commanded what God revealed in this Surah, of manumission, fasting, or feeding, as Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of Salamah ibn Sakhr al-Ansari, who said: I was a man who had been given intercourse with women in a way that no one else had been given. When Ramadan came, I declared a zihar declaration of divorce from my wife until Ramadan had passed, fearing that I might have intercourse with her that night, and I would continue doing that until the day came, and I would not be able to withdraw. While she was serving me at night, something of her was uncovered to me, so I jumped on her. When morning came, I went to my people and told them my story and said: Come with me to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and inform him of my situation. They said: No, by God, we will not do that, for we fear that something will be revealed about us, or that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will say something about us that will remain shameful for us. But you go and do what you want. He said: So I went out until I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him my story. He said to me, You are in this. I said, I am in this. He said, You are in this. I said, I am in this. He said, You are in this. I said, “Yes, here I am. So go with the judgment of God Almighty, for I am patient with Him.” He said, Free a slave. I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said, No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything else this morning. He said, Then fast for two consecutive months. I said, O Messenger of God, did what happened to me happen only because of fasting? He said, Give charity. I said, By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this night full of food and we did not have dinner. He said, Go to the one who gives charity to Banu Ruzayq and tell him to give it to you, so that I may feed sixty poor people from it a wasq of dates, then use the rest of it to help you and your family. He said: So I returned to my people and said, “I found distress and bad opinion among you, but I found spaciousness and blessing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He has ordered for me.” With your charity, give it to me. So they gave it to me. This is how Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi shortened it and declared it good. The context indicates that this story was after the story of Aws ibn al-Samit and his wife Khuwaylah bint Tha’labah, as the context of that and that indicates after reflection. Khasif said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The first person to pronounce zihar from his wife was Aws ibn as-Samit, the brother of Ubadah ibn as-Samit, and his wife Khawlah bint Tha’laba ibn Malik. When he pronounced zihar from her, she feared that it would be a divorce, so she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Aws has pronounced zihar from me, and if we separate, we will perish. I have thrown away my belly from him, and I have become his companion. She was complaining about that and crying, and nothing had been said about that. Then God, the Most High, revealed: “God has certainly heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. Those among you who swear to divorce their wives - they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say an evil word and a lie. And indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who swear to divorce their wives and then go back on what they said - the freeing of a slave before they touch each other. That is what you are admonished by, and God is Acquainted with what you do. But whoever cannot find [a way] - then a fast of two consecutive months before the divorce.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called him and said, Can you afford to free a slave? He said, No, by God, O Messenger of God, I cannot afford it. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gathered for him until he freed a slave on his behalf, then he went back to his family. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and for this reason Ibn Abbas and the majority held what we have said, and God knows best. God the Almighty’s statement, Those of you who swear an oath of divorce against their wives, the root of zihar is derived from the word back. This is because in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them pronounced zihar against his wife, he would say to her, You are to me like my mother’s back. Then in Islamic law, zihar was applied to all other parts by analogy to the back. In the Jahiliyyah, zihar was considered a divorce, so God made it permissible for this nation and made it an expiation, but He did not make it a divorce as they used to do in their Jahiliyyah. This is what more than one of the early generations said. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When a man said to his wife in the pre-Islamic period, You are to me like the back of my mother, she would be forbidden to him. The first person to pronounce zihar in Islam was Aws, and he had a cousin of his called Khuwaylah bint Tha’labah under his care. He pronounced zihar from her, and he was disappointed and said, I see that you are forbidden to me, and she said the same to him. He said, “Then go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” So she went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found a hairdresser combing his hair. He said, O Khuwaylah, we have not been commanded to do anything about your matter. So God revealed to His Messenger, saying, O Khuwaylah, be of good tidings. She said, Good report. So he recited to her, “God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. Those among you who pronounce zihar against their wives are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say an abhorrent word and a lie. But indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving.” * And those who swear off their wives and then go back on what they said, then the freeing of a slave before they touch each other.” She said: And what slave do we have? By God, he cannot find a slave other than me. He said: And whoever cannot find a slave, then a fast of two consecutive months. She said: By God, were it not for the fact that he drinks three times a day, his sight would go away. He said: And whoever cannot afford it, then the feeding of sixty poor persons. She said: From where is it? It is only a meal like it. He said: “So he called for half a wasq thirty sa’s, and a wasq sixty sa’s and said: Let him feed sixty poor persons and let him return to you.” This is a strong chain of transmission and a strange context. Something similar to this has been narrated from Abu Al-A’aliyah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Harawi told us, Ali ibn al-Asim told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, who said: Khawlah bint Dulaij was married to a man from the Ansar, and he was blind, poor, and of bad character. The divorce of the people of the Jahiliyyah was that if a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would say: You are to me like my mother’s back, and she had one or two dependents from him. One day she disputed with him about something, and he said: You are to me like my mother’s back, so she carried her clothes until she entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Aisha’s house, and Aisha was washing the side of his head. She came to him with her dependents and said: O Messenger of God, my husband is blind, poor, has nothing, and of bad character, and I disputed with him about something. He became angry and said: You are to me like my mother’s back, and he did not mean divorce, and I have one or two dependents from him. He said: I do not know of you except that you have become forbidden to him. She said: I complain to God about what has happened to me and my children. Aisha turned and washed the other side of his head, and she turned with him and said: O Messenger of God, my husband is blind, poor and ill-tempered. I have one or two children from him, and I disputed with him about something, and he became angry and said: You are to me like the back of my mother, and he did not mean divorce. She said: He raised his head to me and said: I do not know of anything except that you have become forbidden to him. She said: I complain to God about what has happened to me and my children. Aisha saw the face of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) change, so she said to her: Go away. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained in that state of unconsciousness for as long as God willed. When the revelation ceased, he said: O Aisha, where is the woman? So she called her, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: Go and bring me your husband. So she went running, and she came back and found that he was as she had said: blind, poor and ill-tempered. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to God. God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Those among you who swear to divorce their wives - they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say an evil word and a lie. And indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who swear to divorce their wives and then go back on what they said.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Can you find a slave to free before you touch her? He said: No. He said: Can you not fast for two consecutive months? He said: By Him who sent you with the truth, if I do not eat two or three times, my sight almost goes blind. He said: Can you feed sixty poor people? He said: No, unless you help me. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, helped him and said: Feed sixty poor people. He said: And God transformed the divorce into zihar. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn al-Muthanna on the authority of Abd al-A’la on the authority of Dawud heard Abu Al-Aaliyah, so he mentioned something similar in a shorter context. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ila’ and Zihar were divorces in the pre-Islamic era, so God set a time limit for Ila’ to four months and made expiation for Zihar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a similar manner. Imam Malik provided evidence that the disbeliever is not included in this verse by saying, among you, so the address is to the believers. The majority responded that this was stated in a general manner and has no meaning. The majority provided evidence for it by saying, of their women, that there is no Zihar among the female slaves and they are not included in this address. God the Almighty said: “They are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them.” That is, a woman does not become his mother because of a man saying, You are to me like my mother, or like my mother, or like my mother’s back, or something similar. Rather, his mother is the one who gave birth to him. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And indeed, they say something reprehensible and false, that is, obscene, false speech. But indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving, that is, regarding what happened to you during the time of ignorance. And likewise, regarding what came out of a slip of the tongue, and was not intended by the speaker, as Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) heard a man say to his wife, O my sister, so he said, Is she your sister? This is a denial, but he did not forbid her to him simply because he did not intend it. If he had intended it, she would have been forbidden to him because, according to the correct view, there is no difference between a mother and other mahrams such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and the like. And the Almighty said: And those who pronounce zihar declaration of divorce from their wives and then go back on what they said. The early Muslims and Imams differed regarding what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: Then go back on what they said. Some people said: Going back is to return to the word of zihar and repeat it. This statement is invalid and is the choice of Ibn Hazm and the statement of Dawud. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated it on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Ashja, Al-Farra’ and a group of the people of scholastic theology. Al-Shafi’i said: It is to keep her after zihar for a period during which he can divorce her, but he does not divorce her. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: It is to return to intercourse or resolve to do so, so she is not permissible for him until he expiates with this expiation. It was narrated on the authority of Malik that it means resolving to have intercourse and refraining, and on his authority that it means intercourse. Abu Hanifa said: It is to return to zihar after it was forbidden and the removal of what was the order of the Jahiliyyah. So whenever a man pronounces zihar declaration of divorce from his wife, he has forbidden her with a prohibition that can only be removed by expiation. His companions held this view. Al-Layth bin Sa’d said: Ibn Lahi’ah said: Ata’ told me on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr: Then they go back to what they said. They said, That means they want to return to the sexual intercourse that they had forbidden themselves. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It means intercourse in the vagina. He did not see any harm in intercourse other than the vagina before making expiation. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Before they touch each other. Touching is sexual intercourse. Ata’, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said the same. Al-Zuhri said: He is not allowed to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation. The Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man said: O Messenger of God, I divorced my wife by zihar and had intercourse with her before making expiation. He said: What made you do that, may God have mercy on you? He said: I saw her anklet in the moonlight. He said: Do not go near her until you do what God the Almighty has commanded you. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib sahih. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ikrimah as a mursal. An-Nasa’i said: It is more correct. And the Almighty’s saying: Then the freeing of a slave means the freeing of a complete slave before they touch each other. Here, the slave is absolute and not restricted by faith, and in the expiation for murder, it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, interpreted what was stated here as what was restricted there, due to the unification of the obligation, which is the freeing of a slave. He supported that with what he narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami in the story of the black slave girl, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Free her, for she is a believer. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad and Muslim in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Yasar, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I divorced my wife by zihar, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘before they touch each other’?” He said: I was impressed by that. He said: Keep away until you make expiation. Then Al-Bazzar said: Nothing better than this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ismail bin Muslim spoke about him, and many scholars narrated from him. It contains some jurisprudence, as he only ordered him to make one expiation. God the Almighty says: {This is what you are admonished with} meaning, you are admonished with it. {And God is All-Aware of what you do} meaning, He is All-Aware of what is good for you and All-Knowing of your affairs. God the Almighty says: {But whoever cannot find [the means] - then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. And whoever cannot afford it - then the feeding of sixty poor persons} The hadiths ordering this have been presented previously, as is proven in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan. {That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger} meaning, We have prescribed this for this. God the Almighty says: {And these are the limits set by God} meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them. God the Almighty says: {And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment} meaning, those who do not believe and do not adhere to the rulings of this Shariah. Do not think that they will be saved from the calamity. No, it is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and the hereafter.

When morning came, I went to my people and told them my story and said: Come with me to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and inform him of my situation. They said: No, by God, we will not do that, for we fear that something will be revealed about us, or that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will say something about us that will remain shameful for us. But you go and do what you want. He said: So I went out until I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him my story. He said to me, You are in this. I said, I am in this. He said, You are in this. I said, I am in this. He said, You are in this. I said, “Yes, here I am. So go with the judgment of God Almighty, for I am patient with Him.” He said, Free a slave. I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said, No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything else this morning. He said, Then fast for two consecutive months. I said, O Messenger of God, did what happened to me happen only because of fasting? He said, Give charity. I said, By Him who sent you with the truth, we spent this night full of food and we did not have dinner. He said, Go to the one who gives charity to Banu Ruzayq and tell him to give it to you, so that I may feed sixty poor people from it a wasq of dates, then use the rest of it to help you and your family. He said: So I returned to my people and said, “I found distress and bad opinion among you, but I found spaciousness and blessing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have thrown away my belly from him, and I have become his companion. She was complaining about that and crying, and nothing had been said about that. Then God, the Most High, revealed: “God has certainly heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. Those among you who swear to divorce their wives - they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. The majority responded that this was stated in a general manner and has no meaning. The majority provided evidence for it by saying, of their women, that there is no Zihar among the female slaves and they are not included in this address. God the Almighty said: “They are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them.” That is, a woman does not become his mother because of a man saying, You are to me like my mother, or like my mother, or like my mother’s back, or something similar. Rather, his mother is the one who gave birth to him. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And indeed, they say something reprehensible and false, that is, obscene, false speech. But indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving, that is, regarding what happened to you during the time of ignorance. And likewise, regarding what came out of a slip of the tongue, and was not intended by the speaker, as Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) heard a man say to his wife, O my sister, so he said, Is she your sister? This is a denial, but he did not forbid her to him simply because he did not intend it. If he had intended it, she would have been forbidden to him because, according to the correct view, there is no difference between a mother and other mahrams such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and the like. It was narrated on the authority of Malik that it means resolving to have intercourse and refraining, and on his authority that it means intercourse. Abu Hanifa said: It is to return to zihar after it was forbidden and the removal of what was the order of the Jahiliyyah. Al-Layth bin Sa’d said: Ibn Lahi’ah said: Ata’ told me on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr: Then they go back to what they said. They said, That means they want to return to the sexual intercourse that they had forbidden themselves. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It means intercourse in the vagina. He did not see any harm in intercourse other than the vagina before making expiation. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Before they touch each other. Touching is sexual intercourse. Ata’, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said the same. Al-Zuhri said: He is not allowed to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation. He said: What made you do that, may God have mercy on you? He said: I saw her anklet in the moonlight. He said: Do not go near her until you do what God the Almighty has commanded you. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib sahih. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ikrimah as a mursal. An-Nasa’i said: It is more correct. And the Almighty’s saying: Then the freeing of a slave means the freeing of a complete slave before they touch each other. Here, the slave is absolute and not restricted by faith, and in the expiation for murder, it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, interpreted what was stated here as what was restricted there, due to the unification of the obligation, which is the freeing of a slave. He supported that with what he narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami in the story of the black slave girl, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Free her, for she is a believer. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad and Muslim in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Yasar, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I divorced my wife by zihar, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘before they touch each other’?” He said: I was impressed by that. He said: Keep away until you make expiation. Then Al-Bazzar said: Nothing better than this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ismail bin Muslim spoke about him, and many scholars narrated from him. It contains some jurisprudence, as he only ordered him to make one expiation. God the Almighty says: {This is what you are admonished with} meaning, you are admonished with it. {And God is All-Aware of what you do} meaning, He is All-Aware of what is good for you and All-Knowing of your affairs. God the Almighty says: {But whoever cannot find [the means] - then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. And whoever cannot afford it - then the feeding of sixty poor persons} The hadiths ordering this have been presented previously, as is proven in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan. {That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger} meaning, We have prescribed this for this. God the Almighty says: {And these are the limits set by God} meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them. God the Almighty says: {And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment} meaning, those who do not believe and do not adhere to the rulings of this Shariah. Do not think that they will be saved from the calamity. No, it is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and the hereafter.

So she went running, and she came back and found that he was as she had said: blind, poor and ill-tempered. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to God. God hears your dialogue. Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Those among you who swear to divorce their wives - they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say an evil word and a lie. And indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who swear to divorce their wives and then go back on what they said.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Can you find a slave to free before you touch her? He said: No. He said: Can you not fast for two consecutive months? He said: By Him who sent you with the truth, if I do not eat two or three times, my sight almost goes blind. He said: Can you feed sixty poor people? He said: No, unless you help me. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, helped him and said: Feed sixty poor people. He said: And God transformed the divorce into zihar. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn al-Muthanna on the authority of Abd al-A’la on the authority of Dawud heard Abu Al-Aaliyah, so he mentioned something similar in a shorter context. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ila’ and Zihar were divorces in the pre-Islamic era, so God set a time limit for Ila’ to four months and made expiation for Zihar. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a similar manner. Imam Malik provided evidence that the disbeliever is not included in this verse by saying, among you, so the address is to the believers. The majority responded that this was stated in a general manner and has no meaning. The majority provided evidence for it by saying, of their women, that there is no Zihar among the female slaves and they are not included in this address. God the Almighty said: “They are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them.” That is, a woman does not become his mother because of a man saying, You are to me like my mother, or like my mother, or like my mother’s back, or something similar. Rather, his mother is the one who gave birth to him. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And indeed, they say something reprehensible and false, that is, obscene, false speech. But indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving, that is, regarding what happened to you during the time of ignorance. And likewise, regarding what came out of a slip of the tongue, and was not intended by the speaker, as Abu Dawud narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) heard a man say to his wife, O my sister, so he said, Is she your sister? This is a denial, but he did not forbid her to him simply because he did not intend it. If he had intended it, she would have been forbidden to him because, according to the correct view, there is no difference between a mother and other mahrams such as a sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt, and the like. And the Almighty said: And those who pronounce zihar declaration of divorce from their wives and then go back on what they said. The early Muslims and Imams differed regarding what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: Then go back on what they said. Some people said: Going back is to return to the word of zihar and repeat it. This statement is invalid and is the choice of Ibn Hazm and the statement of Dawud. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated it on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Ashja, Al-Farra’ and a group of the people of scholastic theology. Al-Shafi’i said: It is to keep her after zihar for a period during which he can divorce her, but he does not divorce her. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: It is to return to intercourse or resolve to do so, so she is not permissible for him until he expiates with this expiation. It was narrated on the authority of Malik that it means resolving to have intercourse and refraining, and on his authority that it means intercourse. Abu Hanifa said: It is to return to zihar after it was forbidden and the removal of what was the order of the Jahiliyyah. So whenever a man pronounces zihar declaration of divorce from his wife, he has forbidden her with a prohibition that can only be removed by expiation. His companions held this view. Al-Layth bin Sa’d said: Ibn Lahi’ah said: Ata’ told me on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr: Then they go back to what they said. They said, That means they want to return to the sexual intercourse that they had forbidden themselves. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It means intercourse in the vagina. He did not see any harm in intercourse other than the vagina before making expiation. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Before they touch each other. Touching is sexual intercourse. Ata’, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said the same. Al-Zuhri said: He is not allowed to kiss her or touch her until he makes expiation. The Sunan scholars narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man said: O Messenger of God, I divorced my wife by zihar and had intercourse with her before making expiation. He said: What made you do that, may God have mercy on you? He said: I saw her anklet in the moonlight. He said: Do not go near her until you do what God the Almighty has commanded you. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib sahih. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ikrimah as a mursal. An-Nasa’i said: It is more correct. And the Almighty’s saying: Then the freeing of a slave means the freeing of a complete slave before they touch each other. Here, the slave is absolute and not restricted by faith, and in the expiation for murder, it is restricted by faith. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, interpreted what was stated here as what was restricted there, due to the unification of the obligation, which is the freeing of a slave. He supported that with what he narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami in the story of the black slave girl, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Free her, for she is a believer. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad and Muslim in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Yasar, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I divorced my wife by zihar, then I had intercourse with her before I made expiation. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Did not God, the Most High, say: ‘before they touch each other’?” He said: I was impressed by that. He said: Keep away until you make expiation. Then Al-Bazzar said: Nothing better than this has been narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ismail bin Muslim spoke about him, and many scholars narrated from him. It contains some jurisprudence, as he only ordered him to make one expiation. God the Almighty says: {This is what you are admonished with} meaning, you are admonished with it. {And God is All-Aware of what you do} meaning, He is All-Aware of what is good for you and All-Knowing of your affairs. God the Almighty says: {But whoever cannot find [the means] - then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. And whoever cannot afford it - then the feeding of sixty poor persons} The hadiths ordering this have been presented previously, as is proven in the two Sahihs in the story of the man who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan. {That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger} meaning, We have prescribed this for this. God the Almighty says: {And these are the limits set by God} meaning, His prohibitions, so do not violate them. God the Almighty says: {And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment} meaning, those who do not believe and do not adhere to the rulings of this Shariah. Do not think that they will be saved from the calamity. No, it is not as they claim. Rather, for them is a painful punishment, meaning in this world and the hereafter.
58:5: God Almighty tells us about those who defied God and His Messenger and opposed His law: They were humiliated as those before them were humiliated. That is, they were humiliated, cursed, and disgraced as was done to those who were similar to them before them. And We have sent down clear signs. That is, clear signs that no one would defy or contradict except a disbelieving, wicked, stubborn person. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment. That is, in response to their arrogance in not following God’s law, submitting to it, and submitting to it. Then God the Almighty said: The Day God will resurrect them all - that is, the Day of Resurrection, when God will gather the first and the last on one plain and will inform them of what they did - that is, He will inform them of what they did of good and evil God has recorded it, but they have forgotten it - that is, God has recorded it and preserved it for them, and they have forgotten what they had done and God is Witness over all things - that is, nothing is hidden from Him, nor is anything hidden, nor does He forget anything. Then God the Almighty said, informing about His comprehensive knowledge of His creation, His seeing them, His hearing their speech, and His seeing their place wherever they are, God the Almighty said: Do you not see that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There is not a secret of three - that is, a secret of three but He is their fourth, nor five but He is their sixth, nor fewer than that or more but He is with them wherever they are - that is, He is aware of them, He hears their speech, their secrets, and their private conversations, and His messengers also write down what they privately share with God, with His knowledge and His hearing of it, as God the Almighty said: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations, and that God is Knower of the unseen? God the Almighty said: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down. That is why more than one person has narrated the consensus that what is meant by this verse is the presence and knowledge of God the Almighty, and there is no doubt about what is meant by that. However, His hearing, along with His knowledge of them, encompasses them and His sight penetrates them. He, glory be to Him, is aware of His creation and nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. Then God the Almighty said: “Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.” Imam Ahmad said: He began the verse with knowledge and concluded it with knowledge.

58:8: Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden? The Jews said this, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same, and he added: There was a truce between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews, and whenever a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by them, they would sit whispering among themselves until the believer thought that they were whispering about killing him or about something the believer would dislike. When the believer saw that, he would fear them and leave his way to them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from secret conversation, but they did not stop and returned to secret conversation. Then God Almighty revealed: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden? Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami told us, Sufyan ibn Hamza told me, on the authority of Kathir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Rabih ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: We would take turns with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to spend the night with him, and something would come to him at night and something would appear to him. One night, the people of Nuwaab and the religious police increased in number until we were in groups talking. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us and said, What is this whispering? Were you not forbidden from whispering? We said, “We repent to God, O Messenger of God. We were mentioning the Messiah out of fear of him.” He said, Shall I not tell you of something that I fear most for you? We said, Yes, O Messenger of God! He said, Hidden polytheism is when a man stands up and works for another. This is a strange chain of transmission and it contains some weak narrators. God the Almighty said: And they whisper among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger meaning they speak among themselves about sin which is what is specific to them and aggression which is what is related to others, including disobeying the Messenger and opposing him, which they persist in and advise one another to do. God the Almighty said: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Numair told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Jews entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Death be upon you, O Abu Al-Qasim. Aisha said: And upon you be death. She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Aisha, God does not like obscenity or indecency. I said: Do you not hear them say Death be upon you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Did you not hear me say, ‘And upon you!’ Then God Almighty revealed: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you. In a narration in Sahih, she said to them, Upon you be death, blame, and the curse. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Our prayers regarding them will be answered, but their prayers regarding us will not be answered. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting with his companions, a Jew came to them and greeted them. They returned his greeting, so the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Do you know what he said? They said, Salam O Messenger of God. He said, Rather he said, ‘Samu ‘alaykum,’ meaning, Samu ‘alaykum you will be greeted by your religion. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Return it to him. They returned it to him. The Prophet of God said, Did you say, ‘Samu ‘alaykum?’ He said, Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, If one of the People of the Book greets you, then say, ‘alaykum,’ meaning, alaykum is what you said. The original hadith of Anas is included in Sahih, and this hadith is included in Sahih on the authority of Aisha in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: And they say within themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ That is, they do this and say what they distort of speech and give the impression of greeting, but it is actually an insult inwardly. In addition to this, they say within themselves, “If this man were a prophet, God would punish us for what we say to him inwardly, because God knows what we conceal. If this man were truly a prophet, God would likely hasten our punishment in this world. God the Almighty said, “Hell is sufficient for them,” meaning Hell is sufficient for them in the Hereafter. They will burn therein, so wretched is the destination. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Jews used to say to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Samu ‘alaykum, then they would say within themselves, Why does God not punish us for what we say? So this verse was revealed: And when they come to you, [O Muhammad], and they say within themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ Its chain of transmission is hasan, and they did not include it in their collections. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: The hypocrites would say to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, when they greeted him, “Peace be upon you.” God, the Most High, said: Hell is sufficient for them, which they will burn, and wretched is the destination. Then God, the Most High, said, advising His believing servants not to be like the unbelievers and hypocrites: O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, meaning like the ignorant unbelievers among the People of the Book and those among the hypocrites who supported them in their misguidance, “but confer privately about righteousness and piety. And fear God, to whom you will be gathered,” meaning, He will inform you of all your deeds and words that He has counted against you and will reward you for them. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz and Affan told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, who said: I was holding the hand of Ibn Umar when a man came up to him and said, “How did you hear the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say about private conversation on the Day of Resurrection?” He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God brings the believer close, places His cloak over him, screens him from the people, and makes him confess his sins and says to him: ‘Do you recognize such and such sin? Do you recognize such and such sin? Do you recognize such and such sin?’ Until, when He makes him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he is doomed, He says: ‘I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.’ Then he is given his book of good deeds. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, the witnesses say: ‘These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.’” Bukhari and Muslim Then God the Almighty said: “The private conversation is only from Satan to grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all except by God’s permission. And upon God let the believers put their trust.” That is, the private conversation, which is a secret conversation in which a believer imagines evil, is only from Satan to grieve those who believe, meaning that this only comes from those who are whispering to him as a result of Satan’s instigation and embellishment. To grieve those who believe, that is, to distress them, but it will not harm them at all except by God’s permission. And whoever feels any of that, let him seek refuge in God and put his trust in God, for nothing will harm him, by God’s permission. The Sunnah forbade whispering to one another when it would cause harm to a believer, as Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’ and Abu Mu’awiyah, who said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If there are three of you, then two should not whisper to one another without the third except with his permission, for that will make him sad. Muslim alone transmitted it on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’ and Abu Kamil, both of them on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayoub, with it.

Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz and Affan told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, who said: I was holding the hand of Ibn Umar when a man came up to him and said, “How did you hear the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say about private conversation on the Day of Resurrection?” He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God brings the believer close, places His cloak over him, screens him from the people, and makes him confess his sins and says to him: ‘Do you recognize such and such sin? Do you recognize such and such sin? Do you recognize such and such sin?’ Until, when He makes him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he is doomed, He says: ‘I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.’ Then he is given his book of good deeds. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, the witnesses say: ‘These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.’” Bukhari and Muslim Then God the Almighty said: “The private conversation is only from Satan to grieve those who believe, but it will not harm them at all except by God’s permission. And upon God let the believers put their trust.” That is, the private conversation, which is a secret conversation in which a believer imagines evil, is only from Satan to grieve those who believe, meaning that this only comes from those who are whispering to him as a result of Satan’s instigation and embellishment. To grieve those who believe, that is, to distress them, but it will not harm them at all except by God’s permission. 58:10: Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden? The Jews said this, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same, and he added: There was a truce between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews, and whenever a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by them, they would sit whispering among themselves until the believer thought that they were whispering about killing him or about something the believer would dislike. When the believer saw that, he would fear them and leave his way to them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from secret conversation, but they did not stop and returned to secret conversation. Then God Almighty revealed: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden? Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami told us, Sufyan ibn Hamza told me, on the authority of Kathir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Rabih ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: We would take turns with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to spend the night with him, and something would come to him at night and something would appear to him. One night, the people of Nuwaab and the religious police increased in number until we were in groups talking. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us and said, What is this whispering? Were you not forbidden from whispering? We said, “We repent to God, O Messenger of God. We were mentioning the Messiah out of fear of him.” He said, Shall I not tell you of something that I fear most for you? We said, Yes, O Messenger of God! He said, Hidden polytheism is when a man stands up and works for another. This is a strange chain of transmission and it contains some weak narrators. God the Almighty said: And they whisper among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger meaning they speak among themselves about sin which is what is specific to them and aggression which is what is related to others, including disobeying the Messenger and opposing him, which they persist in and advise one another to do. God the Almighty said: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Numair told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Jews entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Death be upon you, O Abu Al-Qasim. Aisha said: And upon you be death. She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Aisha, God does not like obscenity or indecency. I said: Do you not hear them say Death be upon you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Did you not hear me say, ‘And upon you!’ Then God Almighty revealed: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you. In a narration in Sahih, she said to them, Upon you be death, blame, and the curse. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Our prayers regarding them will be answered, but their prayers regarding us will not be answered. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting with his companions, a Jew came to them and greeted them. They returned his greeting, so the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Do you know what he said? They said, Salam O Messenger of God. He said, Rather he said, ‘Samu ‘alaykum,’ meaning, Samu ‘alaykum you will be greeted by your religion. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Return it to him. They returned it to him. The Prophet of God said, Did you say, ‘Samu ‘alaykum?’ He said, Yes. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, If one of the People of the Book greets you, then say, ‘alaykum,’ meaning, alaykum is what you said. The original hadith of Anas is included in Sahih, and this hadith is included in Sahih on the authority of Aisha in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: And they say within themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ That is, they do this and say what they distort of speech and give the impression of greeting, but it is actually an insult inwardly. In addition to this, they say within themselves, “If this man were a prophet, God would punish us for what we say to him inwardly, because God knows what we conceal. If this man were truly a prophet, God would likely hasten our punishment in this world. God the Almighty said, “Hell is sufficient for them,” meaning Hell is sufficient for them in the Hereafter. They will burn therein, so wretched is the destination. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Jews used to say to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), Samu ‘alaykum, then they would say within themselves, Why does God not punish us for what we say? So this verse was revealed: And when they come to you, [O Muhammad], and they say within themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ Its chain of transmission is hasan, and they did not include it in their collections. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: The hypocrites would say to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, when they greeted him, “Peace be upon you.” God, the Most High, said: Hell is sufficient for them, which they will burn, and wretched is the destination. Do you recognize such and such sin? Do you recognize such and such sin?’ Until, when He makes him confess his sins and he sees in himself that he is doomed, He says: ‘I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.’ Then he is given his book of good deeds.
