58:11: God the Almighty says, educating his believing servants and commanding them to be kind to one another in gatherings: “O you who have believed, when you are told, ‘Make room in gatherings,’” and in gatherings is read as make room, God will make room for you. This is because the reward is of the same kind as the deed, as stated in the authentic hadith: Whoever builds a mosque for God, God will build for him a house in Paradise. And in another hadith: “And whoever makes things easy for one in difficulty, God will make things easy for him in this world and the hereafter. God is with the servant as long as the servant is with his brother.” There are many similar examples of this, and this is why God the Almighty said: make room, God will make room for you. Qatada said: This verse was revealed regarding gatherings for remembrance, because if they saw someone approaching, they would be reluctant to sit with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God the Almighty commanded them to make room for one another. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed on a Friday, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the Suffah on that day, and the place was narrow. He was honoring the people of Badr from the Muhajireen and Ansar. Some people from the people of Badr came and had preceded him to the gatherings. They stood in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy and blessings of God.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) responded to them. Then they greeted the people after that, and they responded to them. They stood on their feet, waiting for space to be made for them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knew what was making them stand, so he did not make space for them. This upset the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said to those around him from the Muhajireen and Ansar who were not from Badr: Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so. He continued to make them stand with the number of people who were standing in front of him from the Muhajireen and Ansar from the people of Badr. This upset those who were made to stand from their seats, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw the dislike on their faces. The hypocrites said: Do you not claim that your companion is just among people? By God, we have never seen anyone treat these people justly. Some people took their seats and wanted to be close to their Prophet, so he made them stand and seated whoever was slow to leave. It reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on a man who makes room for his brother. So after that, they would stand up quickly and make room for their brothers, and this verse was revealed on a Friday. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Imam Ahmad and Ash-Shafi’i said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man should not make another man get up from his seat so that he can sit in it, but make room and spread out. Both of them included it in their Sahihs on the authority of Nafi’. Ash-Shafi’i said: ‘Abd al-Majid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulayman ibn Musa said, on the authority of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “None of you should make his brother get up on Friday, but let him say: ‘Make room,’” in accordance with the conditions of the Sunnah, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa’sa’ah, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Abi Ya’qub, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: A man should not make another man get up from his seat and then sit in it, but make room and God will make room for you. It was also narrated on the authority of Surayj ibn Yunus and Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu’addib, on the authority of Falih, with the same wording: A man should not get up for another man from his seat, but make room and God will make room for you. Ahmad was the only one to narrate it. The jurists differed regarding the permissibility of standing for a newcomer. Some permitted it, citing the hadith, Stand up for your master. Others forbade it, citing the hadith, Whoever likes men to stand up for him, let him take his seat in Hellfire. Others separated and said it is permissible when returning from a journey and for the ruler in his place of authority, as indicated by the story of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) appointed him as a ruler over Banu Qurayzah and he saw him approaching, he said to the Muslims, Stand up for your master. This was only so that his judgment would be more enforceable, and God knows best. As for making it a custom, it is a symbol of the Persians. It was reported in the Sunnah that there was no person more beloved to them than the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When he came, they would not stand up for him because they knew he disliked that. In the hadith narrated in the Sunnah, it is stated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would sit wherever the gathering ended, but wherever he sat, it would be at the front of the gathering. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, would sit from him according to their ranks. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, would sit on his right and Umar on his left, and in front of him would often be Uthman and Ali because they were among those who wrote down the revelation. He would order them to do so, as Muslim narrated from the hadith of Al-A’mash, from Ammarah ibn Umair, from Abu Muammar, from Abu Mas’ud, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say: Let those among you who are wise and wise come closest to me, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. This was only so that they would understand what he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying. For this reason, he ordered those people to stand so that those who had arrived from the Battle of Badr could sit, either because those had fallen short in their duties towards the people of Badr, or so that the people of Badr could take their share of knowledge, as those before them had taken, or as a teaching by putting the best forward. Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara bin Umair Al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abu Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to touch our shoulders during prayer and say: “Stand straight and do not differ, lest your hearts differ. Let those among you who are wise and intelligent be closest to me, then those who come after them, then those who come after them.” Abu Mas’ud said: So today you are more divided. Muslim and the People of the Sunnah narrated it in this way, except for Al-Tirmidhi, through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-A’mash. If this was his command to them in prayer, that the wise and knowledgeable among them should be next to him, then it is more appropriate that this should be done outside of prayer. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Muawiyah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Zahiriyah, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Straighten the rows, align your shoulders, fill the gaps, and be gentle with your brothers, and do not leave gaps for the devils. Whoever joins a row, God will join him, and whoever severs a row, God will sever him.” For this reason, when Ubayy ibn Ka’b, the master of the reciters, reached the first row, he would take a man from him who would be one of the most distinguished people, and he would enter the front row, citing this hadith as evidence: Those of you who are wise and intelligent should sit next to me. As for Abdullah ibn Umar, he would not sit in the place where his companion stood up for him, in accordance with what was stated above in his narration of the hadith that we have mentioned. We will limit ourselves to this amount of the model related to this verse, otherwise its expansion would require another place. In the authentic hadith: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, three men approached. One of them found a space in the circle and entered it. The second sat behind the people, and the third turned away and left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Shall I not tell you about the story of the three? The first sought refuge with God, so God gave him refuge. The second felt shy, so God felt shy of him. The third turned away, so God turned away from him.” Imam Ahmad said: Itab bin Ziyad told us, Abdullah told us, Usamah bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: It is not permissible for a man to separate two people except with their permission. Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid Al-Laithi with it, and Al-Tirmidhi classed it as hasan. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others that they said about the verse: {When it is said to you, Make room in assemblies, then make room, and God will make room for you}, meaning in assemblies of war. They said: The meaning of His saying: {And when it is said to rise, then rise} is: rise up to fight. Qatadah said: {And when it is said to rise, then rise} means if you are called to do something good, then respond. Muqatil said: If you are called to prayer, then rise up to it. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: When they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his house and wanted to leave, each of them would like to be the last one to leave him, as that might be difficult for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he might have a need. So they were commanded that if they were commanded to leave, they should leave, as God Almighty says: And if it is said to you, ‘Go back,’ then go back. God the Almighty says: “God will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” That is, do not think that if one of you makes way for his brother when he comes or if he is ordered to go out and he goes out, that this is a deficiency in his right. Rather, it is an elevation and a rank with God, and God the Almighty will not waste that for him, but will reward him for it in this world and the hereafter. For whoever humbles himself before God’s command, God will raise his status and spread his fame. For this reason God the Almighty says: “God will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” That is, He is Acquainted with who deserves that and who does not deserve it. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Ibrahim told us, Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Amir ibn Wathilah, that Nafi` ibn Abd al-Harith met `Umar ibn al-Khattab in Usfan, whom `Umar had appointed as governor of Mecca. `Umar said to him: Whom have you appointed as your representative over the people of the valley? He said: I appointed Ibn Abza, one of our clients. `Umar said: Have you appointed a client over them? `Umar said: O Commander of the Faithful, he is a reciter of the Book of God, knowledgeable of the inheritance laws, and a judge. `Umar may God be pleased with him said: Your Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: God raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it. Muslim narrated it in this way from al-Zuhri through other chains of transmission, and it was narrated in a similar manner from `Umar through other chains of transmission. I have already mentioned the merits of knowledge and its people and the hadiths that have been narrated on this subject in detail in the explanation of the Book of Knowledge in Sahih al-Bukhari. All praise and thanks be to God.
58:12: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants, if one of them wants to converse privately with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that is, to be able to do so between them, to offer charity before that to purify and sanctify him and make him fit for this position. For this reason, God the Almighty said: That is better for you and purer. Then He the Almighty said: But if you cannot find any, that is, except for the one who is unable to do that due to his poverty, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He only commanded it for the one who is able to do it. Then He the Almighty said: Did you fear to offer charity before your private conversation? That is, were you afraid that this ruling regarding the obligation of charity before conversing with the Messenger would continue? “But since you did not do it and God has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” So the obligation of that was abrogated for them. It was said that no one acted upon this verse before it was abrogated except Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: They were forbidden from holding private conversation with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) until they gave charity, and no one held private conversation with him except Ali ibn Abi Talib, who presented a dinar in charity and gave it in charity. Then he held a private conversation with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) asked him about ten things, and then the permission was revealed. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated on the authority of Mujahid that Ali may God be pleased with him said: There is a verse in the Book of God, the Almighty, which no one before me acted upon, and no one after me will act upon. I had a dinar and exchanged it for ten dirhams. When I held a private conversation with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would give a dirham in charity. It was abrogated, and no one before me acted upon it, and no one after me will act upon it. Then he recited this verse: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity (al-Anfal 2:17). Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ali ibn Alqama al-Anmari, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: What do you think, a dinar? He said: They cannot bear it. He said: Half a dinar. He said: They cannot bear it. He said: What do you think? He said: A barley grain. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: You are indeed insignificant. He said: Then the verse was revealed: Did you fear to offer alms before your private conversations? Ali said: Because of me, God lightened the burden on this nation. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Sufyan ibn Wakee’, on the authority of Yahya ibn Adam, on the authority of Ubaydullah Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Mughirah Ath-Thaqafi, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ali ibn Alqamah Al-Anmari, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, who said: When the verse, O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an amount of charity was revealed, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me, What do you think, a dinar? I said, They cannot afford it. And he mentioned it in full like this. Then he said, This is a hasan ghareeb hadith; we only know it from this source. Then he said, The meaning of his statement, ‘a grain of barley’, is the weight of a grain of gold. Abu Ya’la narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yahya ibn Adam with this same chain of transmission. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, “O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an amount of charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you cannot find [anything], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Muslims used to offer charity before their private conversations, but when zakat was revealed, this was abrogated. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his statement, Then offer charity before your private conversations, was because the Muslims kept asking the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) so much that they became difficult for him. God wanted to make things easier for His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), but when he said that, many of the Muslims became cowardly and stopped asking. After that, God revealed, Did you fear to offer charity before your private conversations? Then since you did not do so and God has turned to you in forgiveness, then establish prayer and give zakat, so God made things easy for them and did not make them difficult. Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about the verse of God the Almighty: Then offer alms before your private conversations that it was abrogated by the verse that follows it: Do you fear to offer alms before your private conversations? until the end of it. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan: The people asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they were constantly begging him, but God weaned them with this verse. If a man among them had a need from the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he could not fulfill it until he offered alms before him. This was very difficult for them, so God revealed the dispensation after that: But if you cannot find [anything], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada, When you confer privately with the Messenger, offer charity before your private conversation. It was abrogated and was only for an hour during the day. And this is how Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Mujahid, Ali said: No one acted upon it except me until it was abrogated, and I think he said: And it was only for an hour.
58:13: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants, if one of them wants to converse privately with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that is, to be able to do so between them, to offer charity before that to purify and sanctify him and make him fit for this position. For this reason, God the Almighty said: That is better for you and purer. Then He the Almighty said: But if you cannot find any, that is, except for the one who is unable to do that due to his poverty, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
